  CONCURRENT JOINT MEETINGS OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF

  OF THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE COMMERCE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
  COMMISSION
The City will be conducting public meeting in –person in the Council Chambers.  To participate in the City of
Commerce ‘public meetings and provide public comments, please follow these steps:

1. Participate in person during the meeting, and submit public comments card if you would like to speak on any
item on the agenda or any other topic.

Watch or Listen: Meetings are broadcast/streamed live on the City of Commerce’s Facebook:

https://www.facebook.com/City-of-Commerce-123903054365151/?ref.  Archived,  on-demand  video  of  each
meeting is maintained on the City’s Facebook as part of the public record.

2. Submit Comments before the Meeting: Members of the public can provide public comment by sending an
e-mail to cityclerk@ci.commerce.ca.us for City Council meetings. Written public comments will be acknowledged
and summarized during the public comment period by the City Clerk or the Mayor.

1.  Pursuant to Government Code §54957.6 the City Council will confer with its labor
  negotiator, Edgar P. Cisneros, with respect to labor negotiations pertaining to:

  A. The Memoranda of Understanding between the City and the City of Commerce
  Employees Association on behalf of the part -time employees.

  B. The Memoranda of Understanding between the City and the City of Commerce
  Employees Association  on  behalf  of  the  mid-management  and  non-management
  full-time employees.

  C. Compensation and benefits for the unrepresented full-time executive management
  employees.

2.  Pursuant to Government Code §54956.8, the City Council will confer with its real
  property negotiator, Edgar Cisneros, with respect to real estate negotiations with:
  A. Wash-Tel Commerce, LLC concerning proposed price and other terms relating
  thereto, comprised of 6329 and 6355 Washington Boulevard, Commerce,
  California, commonly referred to as the Stahl Trust property.

  B. Craig Realty Corporation concerning proposed price and other terms relating
  thereto, comprised of the former Commerce Community Development
  Commission-owned real property located along the Telegraph Road Corridor,
  south of Gaspar Avenue and north of the Commerce Casino [Tubeway Avenue],
  formerly known as 5809, 5819, 5823, 2901/2903, 5933, 5901, 5959, 6000, 6003
  and 6233 Telegraph Road and 2240 Gaspar Avenue; 2311, 2322 and 2366
  Travers Avenue, Commerce, California.

  C. Various parties for 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce CA (APN: 6335-025-901).

PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person
shall make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

3.  Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 16A, and 16B

  and claims set forth in Warrant Registers No. 16A dated April 11, 2023, and

  Attachments:  16 A 2023
  16 B 2023

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Rebollo called meeting to order at 5:08 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any Closed Session items.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION The City Council/Successor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:09 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION The City Council reconvened to Open Session at 6:09 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT Associate Attorney Nvair G. Deukmejian reported on Closed Session items: 

Item #2A was not discussed in the Closed Session.

Items #1, #2.B and #2.C  - staff made a presentation, feedback was provided by the City Council and no reportable action was taken on any of those items.  


6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Rebollo called regular City Council meeting to order at 6:10 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Acting Public Works Director Nila led the Pledge of Allegiance.

INVOCATION Councilmember Altamirano offered the invocation. 

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. A Proclamation Designating the Month of April 2023 as “Autism Awareness Month.” Director of Parks and Recreation Alaniz provided a presentation and spoke about the City and the Commission of Disabilities Access and Opportunities awareness efforts and accommodations provided. 

Mayor Rebollo thanked Parks and Recreation and the commission for all the awareness they provide and for promoting acceptance. Mayor asked to purchase several more books to ruffle to the community.



PUBLIC COMMENT Aaron Fletcher, Kevin Ryan, James Givens, and Cheryl Capoti spoke in support of the energy project that would benefit the City and bring jobs to the community. 

Luz Flores spoke about Winter (Women in Non-Traditional Employment Roles) organization in Commerce and the employment programs they provide to women. Ms. Flores invited COuncilmembers to come and tour their location and get to know about the company. 

Kiana Hernandez, Education Commissioner, spoke about walkability audit, including the bike safety, which is designed for also adults with disabilities.  Commissioner Hernandez invited everyone to participate in the event.   

- walk audit and talked about bike safety concerns and asked for support in carrying the support. 

Gloria Nezahualcoya and Antonia Lupercia asked that the old transportation routes are reinstated as seniors have to walk to the bus stop several blocks. 





CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Vice Mayor Argumedo asked to continue item #10 to the next meeting.  

5.. Joint Agency Agreement for Bridge Maintenance at Telegraph Road over Rio Hondo River

6.. Professional Services Agreement with Stantec Consulting Services Inc. for the Tubeway Re-alignment Study from Smithway Street to Telegraph Road

7.. Traffic Interconnect System Upgrades Project Acceptance

8.. Automated License Plate Readers Lease Agreement with Flock Group Inc.

9.. Home Security Camera Rebate Program

10.. Vehicle Use Policy Amendment

3.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 16A, and 16B

4.. Approval of Minutes

SCHEDULED MATTERS

11.. City Council Reorganization Mayor Rebollo opened nominations for the Mayor. Councilmember Altamirano nominated Vice Mayor Argumedo for the Mayor of 2023-2024, and Councilmember Garcia seconded. The motion was carried by the following vote: 

AYES: Councilmembers Altamirano, Garcia, Lainez, Vice Mayor Argumedo and Mayor Rebollo (5)

Mayor Argumedo opened nominations for the Vice Mayor and nominated Councilmember Altamirano for Vice Mayor. Councilmember Garcia seconded the nomination. The motion was carried by the following vote: 

AYES: Councilmembers Altamirano, Garcia, Lainez, Rebollo and Mayor Argumedo (5)

Mayor Argumedo and Councilmembers thanked outgoing Mayor Rebollo Oralia for her service as a Mayor during 2022-2023, for her professionalism, and leadership. Councilmember Rebollo thanked everyone for their support. 

Mayor Argumedo read two Certificates of Appreciation/Recognition for outgoing Mayor Rebollo from Montebello Unified School District and the City of Maywood. 

Lilian Magana, Montebello Unified School Board Member, and Jennifer Gutierrez, Board Clerk, thanked Mayor Rebollo for providing outstanding public service and all her hard work. 

Mayor Argumedo thanked everyone for the support and for being selected as a Mayor for 2023-2024. 

Matt Johnson from LA County Supervisor Janice Harn's Office congratulated Mayor Argumedo and thanked outgoing Mayor Rebollo for all her work during the past year. 

Johncito Peraza, Field Deputy for the Office of Congressman Robert Garcia, congratulated Mayor Argumedo and recognized outgoing Mayor Rebollo for her term as a Mayor. 


12.. Organizational Assignments for Councilmembers This item was continued to April 25, 2023, City Council meeting.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS There were no reports.

ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 7:11 p.m.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.


Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.
